about: Which tools work as a prompt in an ordinary chatbot (no Claude Code), and what changes there. Read by scripts/render_chatbot_prompts.py, which turns each command or skill file into a chatbot prompt for the landing page. Every command and skill needs a row; fit is full, limited or none.

help.note: Describe your situation in one line and it names the tool to use. It may name a tool that needs Claude Code; the toolkit page and the README in the ZIP list the tools that work in a chat.

quick-ten.note: Describe what you are about to build. It asks the few questions whose answers change the build, then writes a short brief.

simplify.note: Paste the code or the document. It reviews it for redundancy and complexity and proposes simpler versions; it cannot run your tests, so run them yourself before you keep a change.

coa.note: Useful for structured disagreement on a decision. One chatbot plays every council member and the Chair who sums them up, so the members are not independent and their agreement is weak evidence. It cannot read your files: paste the evidence each member should use.

pace.note: Gives you two framings of a task and a review of each. One chatbot writes both framings and both reviews, so their agreement proves little. Paste the task and any source it must check against.

review.note: Paste the document. One chatbot reads it through all three lenses in turn, so the lenses are not independent readers.

audit.note: Paste the document and the text of each source. It checks each cited number against the text you pasted; a source you do not paste is reported as not on file, never as checked.

quarto.note: Paste your notes. It drafts the Quarto source for the deck; you render it yourself with Quarto installed.

bulletproof.note: Paste the code. It writes the tests and the planted defects; you run them and paste the results back, because it cannot run anything.

list-maker.note: Paste a transcript. It writes the numbered, tiered list. It cannot keep the ledger file, so save the list it gives you and paste it back next time to keep the numbers.

step-by-step.note: Paste the list of changes (for example the output of git log --oneline) or a numbered work list. It walks it one item per turn and tracks which items are left.

meeting-breakdown.note: Paste the transcript. One chatbot plays the five agents in turn, so the review steps are not independent. It writes the per-domain plan in the chat rather than beside the transcript.

setup.note: It writes the Claude Code config file the other commands read.

startup.note: It reads your project's summaries and git history on disk.

daily-summary.note: It builds the summary from your git history and the files the session changed.

weekly-summary.note: It aggregates the daily summary files in your project.

commit.note: It reads and writes your git repository.

run-log.note: It reads the run logs other commands write on disk.

improve.note: It audits the Claude Code setup on your machine.

readable.note: It writes text files beside your PDFs for later searches. A chatbot reads an attached PDF directly.

acquire.note: It downloads and extracts files with a script. In a chat, attach the paper and use /audit with its text.

guard-hook.note: It builds and tests Claude Code hooks.

automate.note: It writes a Claude Code skill and script from your session's history.

pcv.note: PCV is a multi-file protocol that runs scripts in your project. Its method is described at https://mgkay.github.io/pcv/.
